affected_claim: School-level randomized parent–teacher meetings identify effects on student outcomes.

affected_claim: Education moderates positive-key responses in the reported direction.

error_verification: Report PDF2–4 and formal corrigendum DOI10.1017/pan.2024.27 acknowledge invalid education coding. Consequence is a secondary substantive direction reversal, not a reversal of the headline.

additional_source_reviews.original_title: Acquiescence Bias Inflates Estimates of Conspiratorial Beliefs and Political Misperceptions
additional_source_reviews.affected_claim: Association between education and susceptibility to acquiescence; not the average randomized effect of question wording.
additional_source_reviews.evidence: Fourteen Lucid2020 respondents have education=-3105, entered as continuous. Dropping these records alone changes education×question-wording association from -0.00005 (p=.02376) to +.02370; Table2 rounds corrected interaction to .024 (SE .005), and .026 (SE .005) for Big Fake items. Categorical recoding is a separate further check. Average wording effect persists; interpretation of education and acquiescence reverses.
additional_source_reviews.date_evidence: Report cover is dated August9,2024; no first-public-disclosure date established. OSF upload is not public-disclosure proof.
additional_source_reviews.limitations: Education codebook unavailable to reviewers; they interpret -3105 as invalid/missing and larger valid codes as greater education. Report isolates deleting invalid observations from later categorical specification; no public date inferred.

original_title: Gender Bias in Parental Attitude: An Experimental Approach
affected_claim: Random assignment supports cross-treatment comparisons of parental gender bias
substantive_consequence: Nonrandom allocation contradicts household randomization and removes experimental identification for cross-arm hypotheses. No demonstrated reversal of overall gender-bias result.

original_title: Disloyal Managers and Shareholder Wealth
affected_claim: Corporate opportunity waiver laws reduce firm innovation
substantive_consequence: Figure 1 interactions absorb the intended event-time variation; remaining variation comes from calendar/fiscal-year mismatch. Corrected reanalysis does not show the claimed innovation drop.
evidence: Figure1 implemented treatment interacted with state-year and industry-year fixed effects, absorbing intended treatment variation; residual identification relies on calendar versus fiscal year mismatch. Corrected stacked specification removes innovation decline. Original sample unavailable; authors dispute substantive consequences and document database-version differences.
evidence_locator: PDF pp.6–7,16–17; author response dp286 pp.4–6
public_date_evidence: SSRN public posting July 30, 2025; author-hosted July 21, 2025 version already documents exact FE and time-indexing errors (https://www.haraldhau.com/wp-content/uploads/GHL_Full-Text.pdf PDF pp.3,14).
limitations: Original analysis sample unavailable. Database revisions and sample changes mean all numerical differences cannot be attributed solely to fixing the code. Author response disputes implications; materiality verified narrowly for Figure 1 identification.

original_title: The Effect of High-Tech Clusters on the Productivity of Top Inventors
affected_claim: IV and event-study evidence for causal cluster-size effects on inventor productivity
substantive_consequence: Instrument first differences mix cities; within-city correction reduces first-stage F from 22–39 to 4–7 and markedly widens IV uncertainty. Missing time-zero interaction creates an event-study discontinuity that disappears after correction. Baseline positive association remains.
evidence: Instrument first differences computed across cities because sorting omits city; corrected within-city IV first-stage F falls from22–39 to4–7 and main IV estimates lose precision. Eventtime-zero coefficient uses un-interacted cluster size instead of interaction; correcting removes discontinuity.
evidence_locator: PDF pp.5–6,11–14; Table 1
public_date_evidence: Dated primary-author blog explicitly documents both coding errors on January 22, 2024. Archived November 16, 2023 PDF exists but writing date alone is not verified public posting.
limitations: Do not equate loss of IV precision with zero effect or assume corrected point estimates all decrease. Earlier public exposure in 2023 remains possible.

original_title: The Welfare Magnet Hypothesis: Evidence from an Immigrant Welfare Scheme in Denmark
affected_claim: Migration response to welfare benefits
substantive_consequence: Stock changes among immigrants aged 30+ conflate migration with residents aging into the group and deaths. Measuring inflows minus outflows reduces the average detrended 2002–2011 decline from about 3,900 to 1,900 people.
evidence: Change in stock of immigrants aged30+ interpreted as net migration but includes existing residents turning30. Comparing actual inflows minus outflows reduces detrended net-flow decline from3900 to1900; separate alternative estimators yield much lower elasticities.
evidence_locator: PDF pp.5,7–8; Figure 1
public_date_evidence: Public author thread retrieved via Bluesky public API records June 18, 2025, 11:24:07 UTC. Specific post explains aging into age-30 stock and inflated net-flow differences; next post explains pretrend distortion. Author PDF committed same day: https://github.com/JopieAdema/JopieAdema.github.io/commit/c0335813741a8a74db7265624f27ef6736257588
limitations: The 1.3 versus 0.28 elasticity comparison changes estimands and models and is not a pure error correction. Residence-based flow data differ from original origin-based stocks; report checks correspondence. March 2025 seminar could be earlier exposure, but title alone does not verify specific disclosed content.

original_title: The CRAVE and ARGE scales for motivation states for physical activity and sedentarism: Brazilian Portuguese translation and single-item versions

substantive_consequence: Brazilian data duplicate nearly half the nominal 1,168 rows. After all cleaning, authors identify 541 valid participants and withdraw the claim that the data provide Brazilian normative values.

original_title: Validation of the CRAVE-C scale in Chinese adults: a four-study examination of competing motivations for physical activity versus rest
affected_claim: Chronic-illness and psychiatric differences in motivations for activity and rest
substantive_consequence: Study 1 contains repeated sessions; Study 2 control sample differs from reported N and some clinical scores exceed the stated scale. Correcting the psychiatric Move comparison reverses its abstract direction; harmonizing coding removes the chronic-illness Rest difference. Draft response withdraws chronic-illness inference because provenance remains unresolved.
evidence: Duplicate control rows and mismatched scoring/sample counts; draft correction withdraws chronic-illness inference and corrects direction of psychiatric Move comparison. Multiple unrecoverable participant links limit other studies.
evidence_locator: dp324 PDF pp.4–5; dp325 PDF pp.4–5,26

original_title: Banning the purchase of sex increases cases of rape: evidence from Sweden
affected_claim: Swedish sex-purchase ban increased reported rape by44–62 percent
substantive_consequence: Treatment dummy is collinear with year fixed effects; Stata regressor order produces the reported coefficient after dropping other terms. The purported RDD effect therefore is not identified by the stated specification. Further bandwidth and implementation errors affect alternatives.
evidence: Treatment-year dummy is collinear with year fixed effects. Stata retains it only by dropping other regressors; variable ordering changes result. Bandwidth for bias estimation used instead of stated treatment-effect bandwidth. Corrected estimates shrink sharply; standard model cannot estimate stated coefficient.
public_date_evidence: dp226 PDF p.4 explicitly recounts posting the March 2024 critique online after contacting author/editor; archived report supports 2024 disclosure. Later editor note and retraction in 2025 do not reset clock.
limitations: Separate literal errors from revised seasonal models and disputed sample changes. Later retraction DOI 10.1007/s00148-025-01114-2 should be retained as a separate event.

original_title: Temperature and Decisions: Evidence from207,000 Court Cases
affected_claim: Warmer days reduce judges granting asylum
substantive_consequence: Weather-location/time matching errors and coding withdrawn applications as judicial denials reduce the estimated temperature effect by roughly two-thirds after correction. Expanding sample years is a separate extension.
evidence: Wrong time zone/weather averaging, wrong geographical court-weather matches, and withdrawn applications counted as judicial rejections. Correction reduces original estimate about two-thirds; reply restores finding using changed Chinese-applicant exclusion. Separate reanalysis/extending sample not conflated with error correction.
evidence_locator: dp227 PDF pp.5,11–12; Spamann 2020/2022 abstract
public_date_evidence: SSRN says Posted August 5, 2020 and abstract already documents coding/data errors and two-thirds reduction; Harvard Discussion Paper 1036 archived July 7, 2020 manuscript.
limitations: Public 2020 date precedes 2022 journal comment. Reply obtains a restored effect after additionally excluding Chinese applicants; do not attribute that changed sample to correction alone.

original_title: Development Effects of Electrification: Evidence from the Topographic Placement of Hydropower Plants in Brazil
affected_claim: Electrification increases HDI and housing values in Brazil
substantive_consequence: IV simulation and estimation use inconsistent Amazon definitions. Additional code omits HDI definition harmonization and includes populations with missing outcomes in aggregation denominators, implicitly treating missing outcomes as zero; correcting these markedly reduces HDI effects.
evidence: Amazon boundary inconsistent between IV simulation and estimation; acknowledged earlier2021 correction. Additional errors omit HDI definition adjustment and include populations of missing-outcome municipalities in denominator, treating missing outcomes as zero; correcting lowers HDI effects substantially.
evidence_locator: PDF pp.8–9,21–22; Table 1
public_date_evidence: SSRN USAEE Working Paper 21-529 states Posted December 10, 2021. Abstract explicitly says inconsistent Amazon demarcations and loss of precision after consistent implementation. Later HDI/aggregation errors are additional disclosures, not necessarily already in this version.
limitations: Earliest material error at article level established in 2021 for inconsistent Amazon definition. Do not date every later HDI/aggregation error to 2021. Random-seed instability is a separate robustness issue; exact first public day may precede SSRN posting.

original_title: Decoding the elite soccer player’s psychological profile
error_type: incorrect reverse scoring of personality items
affected_claim: Elite soccer players exhibit reduced agreeableness, a feature interpreted as potentially advantageous in intense competition.
substantive_consequence: Original low-agreeableness interpretation is materially undermined. Authors’ recalibrated normative comparison reverses direction, but exact corrected original contrast is not validated.
public_date_evidence: DP311 and DP312 I4R title pages explicitly August2026; scoring-error confirmation and consequence appear in public DP312.
earlier_disclosure_search_limit: GitHub critique repository identified but earliest public visibility/version was not established. Do not treat private submission dates as public disclosure.
evidence: Author response identifies incorrect reverse scoring affecting four of six Agreeableness items (and one Openness item), not merely unusual correlations. The original abstract and discussion prominently characterize elite players as less agreeable. Authors acknowledge that the scoring correction substantially changes Agreeableness scores and that their revised personality analysis yields the opposite direction. This materially undermines that original substantive personality claim independently of unresolved broad data-integrity allegations.
evidence_locator: dp312 PDF pp.17,26-28 (especially lines 415–425 and 613–678),63; original abstract/discussion https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11760505/
limitations: Only a small subset of questionnaires was recovered. Authors fit calibration models to that subset and apply them elsewhere, then compare players against German norms instead of original Brazilian controls. Therefore neither the exact corrected effect nor reversal of the original matched-control contrast is independently established. The narrow qualifying error is wrong scoring invalidating an emphasized original trait interpretation; fabrication and global dataset invalidity remain unproven.

original_title: The Effects of Rural Electrification on Employment: New Evidence from South Africa
verification_level: Source-verified independent reading; original code not rerun
affected_claim: Precision and finite upper bound of the IV estimate of rural electrification on female employment in South Africa
substantive_consequence: The report states that Anderson–Rubin confidence intervals labeled 95% were calculated at 90%. Recomputing at 95% yields a lower bound near 1 percentage point and no finite upper bound. The conclusion that the effect is positive remains; the correction removes the bounded magnitude inference.
corrected_direction: Uncertainty expands upward without a finite upper endpoint; positive lower endpoint remains. This is not a demonstrated reversal of the point estimate or sign.
evidence: DP278 PDF p.20, section 4.4, expressly identifies the 90/95 confidence-level coding error and gives the corrected unbounded interval. Appendix Table C2, PDF p.54, labels corresponding finite intervals AR90%, including approximately [0.02,0.25] and [0.02,0.26].
public_date_evidence: Institutional repository explicitly lists Year of Publication: 2025 for I4R DP278 and links its error-containing PDF. Series cover says December 2025; author title page is dated December 18, 2025. These establish the publication year and stated version month, not an exact first-publication day.

earlier_versions_checked.title: Effects of Rural Electrification on Employment: A Comment on Dinkelman (2011)
earlier_versions_checked.finding: No substantiated disclosure of the confidence-level error. PDF p.31 Table A2 itself labels finite intervals AR95%, and its note attributes differences from original [0.05,0.30] to grid precision. It is an earlier identification critique, not the same error disclosure.

Deck labels a plotted interval AR90% on PDF p.35 and discusses weak-IV inference on p.28, but does not substantiate that the original paper mislabeled 90% as95%. Cannot treat this as verified public error disclosure.
Checked for confidence-level/error discussion; no90/95 or unbounded-interval disclosure found. This is not proof that every historical version lacked it.

later_source.finding: Later SSRN version; not earliest given institutional 2025 source.

limitations: No independent numerical reproduction of the original Stata confidence-set inversion. Treat the precise corrected endpoint as report-based. Source p.20 summarizes finite ranges approximately; original [0.05,0.30] grid and replicated [.02,.25]/[.02,.26] grids should not be conflated. Exclusion restriction, collider bias and road-access robustness are distinct, disputed identification questions. Exact earliest public date remains unresolved; 2020 criticism must not be used as this error event. No formal correction was established in this targeted search.

original_title: The motion-silencing illusion depends on object-centered representation
precise_operation: Using independent-measures ANOVAs for within-subject experiments and analyzing unfiltered RTs despite stated exclusions; Exp2b mean difference misreported as confidence-interval lower bound.

reply_or_dispute: No original-author reply in acquired attachments.
disclosure_date_evidence: Not independently verified. Manuscript/upload dates not used as public exposure.
recommendation: Do not add to significant-error exposure cohort without independent consequence and disclosure adjudication.

verification_scope: Lead and independent reviewers checked the specified source passages and available replies. Original data and code were not independently rerun.
original_title: Schooling and Labor Market Consequences of School Construction in Indonesia: Evidence from an Unusual Policy Experiment
materiality_scope: Hold pending claim-specific materiality review. The reduced-form increase is documented; its substantive importance and the error-only change in the headline IV return require further adjudication. Do not attribute coefficient changes to clustering.
error: Transcription discrepancies in historical regency-level data affect the treatment intensity for about 10% of regencies.
affected_claim: Magnitude and precision of the schooling-construction effect on wages.
corrected_direction: The reported unweighted reduced-form coefficient increases from 0.0147 to 0.0187 after the data corrections. Clustering changes its uncertainty, not its coefficient. Subsequent weighting and weak-IV inference are separate changes; materiality for the substantive claims remains unresolved in this review.
evidence_locator: DP015 PDF pp.6 and13–15, especially Table1 unweighted reduced-form column; annotated original-source reconstruction linked by the report.
public_date_evidence: I4R issue cover January 2023 substantiates this version; earlier error-specific public circulation has not been established.
dispute_status: Data reconstruction is documented by the critic; broader weak-IV, weighting and identification claims are separate from the transcription mistakes.
cohort_recommendation: Hold pending claim-specific materiality review. The reduced-form increase is documented; its substantive importance and the error-only change in the headline IV return require further adjudication. Do not attribute coefficient changes to clustering.

cohort_recommendation: Verified errors with unresolved substantive materiality; keep alternative clustering and removal of May separate from literal corrections.

original_title: A Shot at Economic Prosperity: Long-Term Effects of India’s Childhood Immunization Program on Earnings and Consumption Expenditure
materiality_scope: Include as a material statistical-identification error, with scope limited to the stated rollout-based causal interpretation.
error: District-by-age fixed effects absorb the intended rollout comparison; remaining constructed treatment variation depends on interview timing during the survey.
affected_claim: A causal effect of infant vaccination exposure on adult wages and household consumption.
corrected_direction: Survey-time trends also occur in untreated older cohorts. Controlling survey month removes most of the reported associations. The displayed sequence bundles preliminary data/weighting changes and is not an isolated coding repair or proof of zero vaccination benefit.
evidence_locator: DP103 PDF pp. 5–8, Table 1; arXiv 2401.11100v1 abstract and identification discussion.
public_date_evidence: The arXiv version history dates v1 to January 2024; the cached v1 contains the survey-timing identification criticism. January 20 is a submission timestamp, not asserted as the public announcement day. The March 2024 I4R version is later.
dispute_status: The 2026 author-reply abstract acknowledges partial survey-time dependence and loss of the consumption result under revised specifications, but defends inflation-adjusted male wage effects and disputes the permutation exercise. Full reply PDF not retrieved; claims are limited to its official search-indexed abstract.
cohort_recommendation: Include as a material statistical-identification error, with scope limited to the stated rollout-based causal interpretation.

later_author_response.verification_scope: Official SSRN search-indexed abstract independently read by lead and second reviewer; direct page returned 403 and full PDF was not acquired.
later_author_response.interpretation: Reply retains a male wage benefit; the critique is not evidence that vaccination had no benefit.

materiality_scope: Include as a material numerical correction; do not attribute the broader alternative-specification range to this error alone.

cohort_recommendation: Include as a material numerical correction; do not attribute the broader alternative-specification range to this error alone.

verification_scope: Lead and independent reviewers checked the specified source passages and available replies. Original data and code were not independently rerun.
original_title: Examining Inequality in the Time Cost of Waiting
materiality_scope: Include for a demonstrated change to the focal adjusted-gap magnitude, including a strengthening correction; no claim of an overturned income or race conclusion.
error: Negative missing-income codes were classified as low income; several regressions also omitted the survey weights promised in the article.
affected_claim: The magnitude of the adjusted waiting-time gap between low- and high-income respondents.
corrected_direction: The missing-income correction alone increases the adjusted gap from 0.371 to 0.518 minutes, and the gap conditional on waiting from 5.834 to 7.017. Adding the omitted weights gives 0.626 and 7.518. The direction survives and strengthens.
evidence_locator: DP243 PDF pp. 8–10 and 28/Table 3; author reply DP244 PDF pp. 6–8. Table 3 checkmarks and body identify operations; its note reverses columns 2/3 descriptions.
public_date_evidence: I4R issue cover July 2025; July 2 manuscript date is not independently verified public availability.
dispute_status: Authors acknowledge missing-income and weighting errors but characterize their effects as modest. Larger robustness changes also alter the definition of waiting and must be kept separate.
cohort_recommendation: Include for a demonstrated change to the focal adjusted-gap magnitude, including a strengthening correction; no claim of an overturned income or race conclusion.
source_reporting_discrepancy: The report prose attributes 69%/29% increases to the missing-income fix, but those approximate ratios compare columns 1/3 and combine that fix with weighting. The missing-income-only contrasts are columns 1/2.

affected_claim: Arrest and conviction rates deter terrorism; charge rates increase terrorism; sentence length has no deterrent effect.
materiality_scope: Post-publication editorial review concluded that the article conclusions were unsupported by the analyses; this is more than a shift in statistical significance.

quantitative_consequence.outcome: DVSin remains the outcome in the disclosed-method columns of Table S2.
quantitative_consequence.warning: These contrasts change regressors and samples; they are not an isolated IHS(y+1) correction. The 292 distinct positive stored outcomes at zero attack rates cannot be attributed solely to the admitted addition of one from the inspected evidence.

corrected_direction: No isolated corrected effect of the acknowledged transformation is established.

Use the supported public year 2024, not the 2026 journal publication/retraction or the PDF cover date alone.

dispute_status: Authors accept responsibility for coding errors and agree to retraction, but dispute the other criticisms.
